newsitem.title: USA: Simpson jury ends day without decision on damages.
newsitem.headline: Simpson jury ends day without decision on damages.

text.p: Jurors in O.J. Simpson's civil trial deliberated for about two hours Friday but failed to reach a decision on whether to force him to pay punitive damages in the deaths of his ex-wife and her friend.

Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki ordered the jury to return to court Monday to continue their efforts, a court spokeswoman said. The panel reached a verdict Tuesday blaming the former football star for the murders and slapping him with $8.5 million in compensatory damages.
Before sending jurors off for their second round of deliberations, the judge instructed them to reach their decision "without passion or prejudice."

Jurors met briefly behind closed doors after hearing an impassioned plea from plaintiffs' attorney Daniel Petrocelli, who urged them to impose stiff punitive damages and declare to the world that "You cannot kill two people and get away with it."
But defense attorney Robert Baker contended that Simpson had already been punished enough and said anything more would effectively "destroy" his client.
Simpson was acquitted in October 1995 in the murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman, but the victims' families pressed ahead with a wrongful-death lawsuit in civil court.
